title: When Rough Data Helps: A Phase Transition in Convergence Rates for Kernel Recovery in Integral Operators
summary: Learning kernels in operators from data is a fundamental task that arises in nonlocal continuum mechanics, operator learning, and interacting particle systems. A central question is how the roughness of input data impacts the accuracy of kernel recovery. We quantify the roughness of the input data via its spectral decay exponent and analyze how it determines the degree of ill-posedness of the inverse problem and, consequently, the convergence rates of the Tikhonov-regularized estimator in the small-noise limit.
